items.title: Liesegang Rings
items.author: surprisetalk
items.summary: Last time I write about trying to find phenomena where the physics might stay the same as you shrink down the dimensions. Another one of the themes of the
items.text:
Last time I write about trying to find phenomena where the physics might stay the same as you shrink down the dimensions. Another one of the themes of the independent science society is to figure out how to create complex phenomena worth experimenting with on tabletop.

Previously I demonstrated Rayleigh Bernard convection cells with Mica powder and oil, where I saw cell-like devisions in liquid when I applied a temperature gradient. This was an example of non-equilibrium , self organising phenomena due to the application of a temperature gradient. I've preciously tried and failed to do other things like the Briggs Rauscher reaction, which is a (safer) example of an oscillating chemical reaction.

With regards to complex phenomena, I am trying to figure out which variables actually matter through both math and physical experiments, which is hard. In the case of convection cells, we have variables like the thickness of the liquid layer, the temperature gradient, the size of the container, amongst other things. And these ideas are something I want to get around to understanding myself in this lab.

Another piece of complex phenomena that caught my eye is Liesegang rings. These are rings that form in a gel according to a spacing that goes like (1 + p)^n, which is a geometric series. You can get them through a bunch of different waysHere is what they look like, images taken from this really cool website on Liesegang ring models.

You can see quite clearly the spacing going in a geometric pattern in this one with magnesium hydroxide.

Why do I find this interesting? When reading books about embryology, like the Triumph of The Embryo, I got interested in how chemical reactions give rise to patterning in some animals. I also find that the theory of patterning in chemical reactions is mathematically rich as well, something which I'm trying to understand more through the lens on non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. The aesthetics of these things are just mesmerising. Even though liesegang rings aren't the mechanism behind animal patterning, you still can't help but marvel at what goes on behind the scenes.

Here's a page out of 'A Field Guide To the Birds of Malaysia'.

And to the best of my knowledge, the mechanisms behind Liesegang rings haven't really been fully resolved yet. Which puts this in prime territory to try and replicate some of this stuff at home.

I had a think about trying to replicate Liesegang rings using Potassium dichromate and silver nitrate, which seems to yield the brightest rings. But when I was shopping for potassium dichromate on sigma aldrich and then realised that it was carcinogenic, with inhalation risk. So not really that appropriate for homelab style stuff...

And then the other example on the Liesegang website was using a gel soak of magnesium hydrochloride with ammonia, but I also found the ammonia quite sketchy since the concentrations looked high.

So then I was looking around with Gpt Sol to try and find some safer versions, along with reagants that were more available. So then I came across a paper by Chopard in 1999 which managed to create Liesgang rings out of agar jelly (safe), magnesium chloride (bath salts) and sodium hydroxide. Sodium hydroxide is called caustic soda and can be bought from stores. It's corrosive but doesn't have fumes and I previously used it trying to make quantum dots at home.

Here are photos of the Liesegang rings from the Chopard 1999 paper

I tried the following recipe to make the rings with NaOH, shown in the image on the right.

The reagents were pretty cheap as well, here is th e complete list with the estimated costs from Claude. Again to stress, most of these available pretty readily out there! I would really like to make chemical network research more accessible to home experimentation,

I got Sol to tell me the concentrations and procedure to replicate the paper.

Here is my first attempt. And spoiler alert, it's a fail and I couldn't get the bands to separate properly for some reason. But I think it's just as important to share failures along with successes in the spirit of being a transparent independent scientist so here goes...

Embarassingly the fiddliest part of all this was trying to get the agar jelly nice and smooth so that the gel wouldn't be cloudy, so that I could see the banding.

I first tried to mix 1.5g of agar powder with 90ml and then put it in my magnetic stirrer and heater, but I only managed to get the agar to a temperature of 60C, which isn't enough to fully dissolve the agar powder - you need to get it to near boiling for it to dissolve properly.

It was much quicker and easier to get the agar to 90C temperature by putting it in a microwave for 40s at 900W. You can get agar from any old food shop or on amazon. I used a basic cooking temperature probe to test that it got to temperature.

Putting it into the microwave for 40s managed to get it up to the right temperature for dissolution - here it's 94C.

I then kept the agar warm on my magnetic stirrer at 60C.

And then after that I prepared 2g of Magnesium Chloride Hexahydrate in 98ml of water and then put it in the agar jelly

Stirring it and getting the bubbles out

And then I put it in some test tubes and let it cool, in tubes of 20g each

I then let the MgCl soaked tubes rest for 90 minutes until it became a gel.

After that I put 1g of NaOH in 50ml of water solution, this is corrosive so be careful

And then i poured the NaOH solution into the gel soak.

And then I did this with 3 test tubes and then left one alone.

I left it for 10 hours and here's what I got. As you can see there is a white precipitate interface, which is promising. But I don't see the band structures that I so desperately want to see!

B. Chopard, M. Droz, J. Magnin, Z. Rácz, and M. Zrinyi, "Liesegang Patterns: Effect of Dissociation of the Invading Electrolyte," J. Phys. Chem. A 103 (10), 1432–1436 (1999). ACS · preprint arXiv:cond-mat/9809385.

Liesegang ring experiments and models, insilico.hu.

L. Wolpert, The Triumph of the Embryo (Oxford University Press, 1991).

Lim Kim Seng, Lim Kim Chuah, and Yong Ding Li (illus. Dana Gardner), A Field Guide to the Birds of Malaysia, including Sabah and Sarawak (John Beaufoy Publishing). NHBS.

And then the other example on the Liesegang website was using a gel soak of magnesium hydrochloride with ammonia, but I also found the ammonia quite sketchy since the concentrations looked high.

So then I was looking around with Gpt Sol to try and find some safer versions, along with reagants that were more available. So then I came across a paper by Chopard in 1999 which managed to create Liesgang rings out of agar jelly (safe), magnesium chloride (bath salts) and sodium hydroxide. Sodium hydroxide is called caustic soda and can be bought from stores. It's corrosive but doesn't have fumes and I previously used it trying to make quantum dots at home.
https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!TnFC!,w_32,h_32,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack.com%2Fimg%2Favatars%2Fdefault-light.png
Here are photos of the Liesegang rings from the Chopard 1999 paper

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!thCw!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F330ef220-a7bb-4527-99f4-867c8bae2c5f_799x536.png
I tried the following recipe to make the rings with NaOH, shown in the image on the right.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!UECu!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6816fac4-a5a0-44e8-991f-7cf610679fb2_796x265.png

The reagents were pretty cheap as well, here is th e complete list with the estimated costs from Claude. Again to stress, most of these available pretty readily out there! I would really like to make chemical network research more accessible to home experimentation,

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!TaC4!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4fe9eea6-2ab8-4b5a-a262-57a3fc0f3d16_1314x554.png
I got Sol to tell me the concentrations and procedure to replicate the paper.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!P5Kd!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F9c242c68-a366-48a3-8c87-2b02e2a0e2cd_814x614.png

Here is my first attempt. And spoiler alert, it's a fail and I couldn't get the bands to separate properly for some reason. But I think it's just as important to share failures along with successes in the spirit of being a transparent independent scientist so here goes...
Embarassingly the fiddliest part of all this was trying to get the agar jelly nice and smooth so that the gel wouldn't be cloudy, so that I could see the banding.

I first tried to mix 1.5g of agar powder with 90ml and then put it in my magnetic stirrer and heater, but I only managed to get the agar to a temperature of 60C, which isn't enough to fully dissolve the agar powder - you need to get it to near boiling for it to dissolve properly.

It was much quicker and easier to get the agar to 90C temperature by putting it in a microwave for 40s at 900W. You can get agar from any old food shop or on amazon. I used a basic cooking temperature probe to test that it got to temperature.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!qe36!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0f331ee8-34b0-4970-993b-e1943049ae95_4032x3024.jpeg

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!oOhb!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5b89bd42-92e4-4b2d-a616-3e2c41abe20b_3024x4032.jpeg

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!LDYH!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F93352624-9b11-4f35-a5f6-4325deb234c1_3024x4032.jpeg
Putting it into the microwave for 40s managed to get it up to the right temperature for dissolution - here it's 94C.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!7omY!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fcb49c8d5-ae14-4189-bee0-a82f4f42bbfa_4032x3024.jpeg
I then kept the agar warm on my magnetic stirrer at 60C.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!G9Js!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_lossy/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd2397b83-107f-44c3-9bea-bbb99d2e7575_360x203.gif
And then after that I prepared 2g of Magnesium Chloride Hexahydrate in 98ml of water and then put it in the agar jelly

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!nHkN!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fa56d46e9-4fd9-41ca-93dd-0d3039fca6d8_4032x3024.jpeg

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!KQNE!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_lossy/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F158f0619-4d08-47ed-953d-f8ca9c17e045_360x203.gif

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!d31p!,w_32,h_32,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F1d7647f6-9b26-4368-9e5f-68562416d87c_321x321.jpeg
Stirring it and getting the bubbles out

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!5l2Z!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_lossy/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F9252a56d-9506-4d68-afbf-417bdbd71354_360x203.gif
And then I put it in some test tubes and let it cool, in tubes of 20g each

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!JVXO!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Febc52350-0abb-43ad-885e-8cf5c638d394_3024x4032.jpeg

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!rJhp!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4aa9ec79-c3fa-479c-858c-7947586593e4_4032x3024.jpeg
I then let the MgCl soaked tubes rest for 90 minutes until it became a gel.
After that I put 1g of NaOH in 50ml of water solution, this is corrosive so be careful

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!AXzN!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe1b7f3e0-5b6f-4908-804c-ebea665daa8c_3024x4032.jpeg
And then i poured the NaOH solution into the gel soak.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Jkj4!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_lossy/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F2a022296-35f7-4cb1-99be-fcfd1b6f7d13_380x676.gif

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!AJci!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_lossy/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5dccd69c-e392-40b6-8823-b6ea0d686c6f_380x676.gif

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!RI47!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_lossy/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4d6762ba-b62c-440e-8873-86577e01dae0_380x676.gif
And then I did this with 3 test tubes and then left one alone.

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!lpyP!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7619b564-4452-42cd-9531-8f24c5a32911_4032x3024.jpeg
I left it for 10 hours and here's what I got. As you can see there is a white precipitate interface, which is promising. But I don't see the band structures that I so desperately want to see!

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!wBaK!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd4210ee7-0ab9-45a6-aa96-e58a0f1bfb15_3024x4032.jpeg

看到华为三星折叠机受关注后，库克推动苹果加速研发折叠屏 iPhone

据彭博社记者 Mark Gurman 报道，苹果研发折叠屏 iPhone 的历程已历时近十年，该设备售价预计将超过 2000 美元，标志着苹果近 20 年来最大的设计变革。

报道披露，苹果对折叠设备的关注可追溯至 2020 年前后。彼时苹果 CEO Tim Cook 在结束一次亚洲之行后，对折叠屏手机这一新兴品类表现出了异乎寻常的积极态度。

在走访中国等亚洲地区的行程中，Tim Cook 观察到越来越多消费者开始使用来自三星电子、华为等手机厂商的折叠屏设备。这次见闻让他确信苹果必须推出自家的折叠产品，并随即推动公司加速在这一新兴市场的研发步伐。

OpenAI 发布 Navier–Stokes 千禧年难题候选解，等待数学界检验

OpenAI 9 月 8 日公布一份 Navier–Stokes 存在性与光滑性问题的候选解，同时发布了数学论文和 Lean 形式化证明。公司称，这份证明给出了光滑三维不可压缩流体在有限时间内形成奇点的构造，对应克莱数学研究所问题表述中的 C 和 D 类情形。

OpenAI 称，证明由一个能力高于 GPT-6 Astra 的内部模型完成，系统一度协调约 1 万个并发 Agent。从启动到得到候选解用时约 88 小时，随后由 GPT-6 Astra 花费 17 小时完成 Lean 形式化和验证；Navier–Stokes 项目共产生约 270 万条代理消息和 1300 亿个输出 token。

这项工作也牵出了同期的 Euler 方程研究争议。纽约大学数学教授 Tristan Buckmaster 质疑 OpenAI 是否利用了他与 Anthropic 研究人员 Levent Alpöge 在 Codex 中的项目数据。OpenAI 称求解过程没有访问具体用户数据，但不能完全排除去标识化使用数据曾参与模型改进；双方公开的证明所针对的问题也并不相同。

这份候选解尚未经过全球数学界的独立检验。按克莱数学研究所规则，一项解答需先在合格出版物发表，至少经过两年严格审查并获得广泛认可，才会进入奖项考虑程序。OpenAI 称无意为该结果申请奖项。

🔗 相关阅读：刚刚，OpenAI 宣布攻克千禧年难题，清华姚班传奇陈立杰：不可思议的时代

DeepSeek Flash 系列 9 月 10 日起降价，V4.1 Flash 同步开启内测

DeepSeek 将于 9 月 10 日 12:00 起大幅调整 flash 系列模型定价，闲时输入价格从每百万 token 1.5 元降至 1 元，闲时输出价格从 4.5 元降至 4 元，闲时缓存价格从 0.05 元降至 0.02 元；高峰时段价格为闲时价格的 2 倍。

与此同时，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 中间版本已开放内测。参与内测的 API 用户无需更改 base_url，将模型名切换为「deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910」即可调用，当前计费与 DeepSeek V4 Flash 相同，单账号最多支持 20 并发请求。

该模型 ID 中的失效日期为 9 月 10 日，属短期内测版本，尚未替换官网 API 文档中的正式 V4 Flash 型号，新版本采用不同的模型架构，原生支持多模态，本轮测试重点为能力、生成速度和推理成本。

🔗 相关阅读：刚刚，DeepSeek 新模型突然上线，Flash 的模型，Pro 的野心

两部门要求车企定期报告供应商账期，重点企业每年接受评估

工业和信息化部、市场监管总局 9 月 7 日发布通知，进一步规范汽车企业向供应商支付采购货物、工程和服务等款项。车企需建立供应商账款支付管理制度，并在每年 7 月底和次年 1 月底前分别提交半年度、年度执行情况报告。

工信部将委托第三方机构每年开展一次调研评估，对名单内重点车企实现全覆盖。评估会查阅企业文件和数据、核验现场并访谈员工，关注账期、支付方式及占比、应付账款规模等信息，结果将公开发布。

对于应付账款规模较大、故意拉长账期或被中小企业投诉较多的车企，主管部门将约谈并督促整改；涉及违法违规的，将依法处理。此前行业在 2025 年发起「60 天账期承诺」，此次通知把企业报告、第三方评估、投诉核查和执法衔接写入常态化管理流程。

小米中折叠「卖爆了」，首销较上代大折叠增长 310%

小米集团副总裁、CMO 许斐 9 月 8 日表示，小米 18 Fold 首销较上代大折叠增长 310%。这款中折叠手机前一晚发布，起售价为 10999 元，是小米目前定位最高的手机产品。

曝微信 PC 版接入 AI 助手「小微」，可操作聊天与小程序

微信开始在 PC 版测试 AI 助手「小微」。它能查看朋友圈、发送消息、发起语音和视频通话，也能在聊天中回答文件内容；视频文件和定时消息暂不支持。

「小微」还能调用小程序完成订餐等服务，涉及支付时会交由用户确认。微信内置浏览器的「元宝总结」入口也被替换为「问 AI」，可继续围绕当前网页提问。

面向开发者的能力包括在 PC 端开发和调试小程序、生成体验版。个性化推荐默认关闭，用户可在设置中单独开启；目前没有提供关闭「小微」入口的选项。

蔚来与云南交投新一批高速换电站投运，覆盖 5 条高速双向服务区

蔚来能源与云南交投 9 月 8 日宣布，双方新一批共建高速换电站已全面投入运营。站点分别落在 G5621 昆楚大高速地索坪、G85 银昆高速会泽、G78 汕昆高速师宗、G5 京昆高速元谋和 G8511 昆磨高速通关服务区，5 处服务区均完成双向布点。

这是双方继 2024 年首批合作后的新一轮投运。新站点连接滇中、滇东、滇西和滇南主要通道，补齐省内跨区域、长距离行程中的高速换电节点。双方后续还将推进高速「光储充换」综合能源站和零碳服务区。

截至 9 月 8 日，蔚来称其已建成 9328 座充换电站，其中换电站 4075 座、充电站 5253 座，配备 30284 根充电桩；累计完成超 1.2 亿次换电服务，充换电服务合计超 2 亿次。

DeepSeek 新开约 150 个工程岗位，聚焦后端与 Agent 弹性计算

DeepSeek Harness 团队负责人崔添翼 9 月 7 日公开招聘约 150 人。这批名额主要面向有 2 至 10 年经验的工程师，也接受应届生和初入行从业者；工作地点以北京为主，部分岗位可选杭州。

招聘集中在服务端开发和 Agent 弹性计算研发两类岗位。前者覆盖大模型研究平台、Agent 框架组件、研发效率基建、DeepSeek API、线上服务和数据工程；后者包括平台开发维护与底层系统调优。本轮没有单列 AI 研究岗位。

崔添翼解释称，数据、机器与容器、训练和评测任务、Agent 环境以及用户请求都在增长，原有后端系统需要升级、维护甚至重写。此前 6 月，DeepSeek 曾宣布计划将各部门规模至少扩大一倍；此次招聘的岗位范围更集中。

高通与亚马逊达成多代定制芯片合作，覆盖 AI 推理与 1.6T 光互联

💡 梁琛奇：AI 娱乐产品要让消费过程实时使用算力

字节跳动前 AI 产品团队 Flow 负责人梁琛奇接受《晚点》采访时表示，AI 娱乐产品若只降低内容生产成本，产出的短剧、漫画或视频仍会回到既有平台；新的独立平台需要让用户在消费过程中实时与模型互动，并获得过去不存在的长尾反馈。

他把 AI 娱乐的成立条件归纳为成本、模态和用户习惯。DeepSeek-R1 之后，推理成本继续下降；图片和视频模型跨过可用门槛；用户也已经通过 ChatGPT、豆包等产品学会与 AI 交互。基于这些变化，他判断娱乐产品可以从静态生成转向一边消费、一边生成图片、视频或玩法。

梁琛奇创办的「动念引线」正在同时开发和测试七八个产品，由一两人的小组在两周至一个月内做出 Demo，再按真实用户信号决定关停或追加资源。其首款产品「松果时刻」可把照片和文字扩展为带配音、配乐和简单动画的多图故事；团队下一步会把内容收向特定人群，并尝试让消费端也实时调用模型。

他认为，AI 娱乐仍离不开人的主观表达：模型擅长根据用户偏好生成「熟悉感」，真正的惊喜和内容多样性则来自创作者。产品成立需要同时满足新颖、长期、高频和不易厌倦，并在留存与使用频次上形成可持续信号。

Gibney 曾凭《驶向阴霾的出租》获得奥斯卡最佳纪录长片奖，也执导过《安然：房间里最聪明的人》《拨开迷雾：山达基教与信仰囚笼》和 Steve Jobs 纪录片《史蒂夫·乔布斯：机器人生》。他表示，新片不会简单裁定 Musk「好或坏」，而是考察其权力如何运作。

《Musk》将在 10 月 16 日由 Bleecker Street 于北美院线上映，之后登陆 HBO 和 HBO Max；威尼斯之后还会在多伦多电影节展映。

《世界之巅》上线，回望世贸中心顶层餐厅的 25 年

40 分钟纪录短片《世界之巅》（Top of the World）于 9 月 8 日上线 CNN。影片改编自 Tom Roston 的非虚构作品，由《女大法官金斯伯格》和《茱莉亚》的导演 Betsy West、Julie Cohen 执导，回顾世贸中心北塔 106、107 层餐厅 Windows on the World 的 25 年历史。

影片从 1970 年代餐厅开业讲起，记录其在股市周期中的起落、1993 年世贸中心爆炸案后的恢复，以及 2001 年原定举行的 25 周年庆典。餐厅当时有 400 多名员工，来自 20 多个国家，使用约 60 种语言；片中多位厨师、侍者和管理者讲述各自经历。

在 9·11 恐怖袭击中，Windows on the World 的 79 名员工和 91 名顾客遇难。影片此前于 8 月 28 日至 9 月 3 日在纽约限量上映，目前可通过 CNN 网站和应用观看。

OpenAI 发布 Navier–Stokes 千禧年难题候选解，等待数学界检验
OpenAI 9 月 8 日公布一份 Navier–Stokes 存在性与光滑性问题的候选解，同时发布了数学论文和 Lean 形式化证明。公司称，这份证明给出了光滑三维不可压缩流体在有限时间内形成奇点的构造，对应克莱数学研究所问题表述中的 C 和 D 类情形。
OpenAI 称，证明由一个能力高于 GPT-6 Astra 的内部模型完成，系统一度协调约 1 万个并发 Agent。从启动到得到候选解用时约 88 小时，随后由 GPT-6 Astra 花费 17 小时完成 Lean 形式化和验证；Navier–Stokes 项目共产生约 270 万条代理消息和 1300 亿个输出 token。
这项工作也牵出了同期的 Euler 方程研究争议。纽约大学数学教授 Tristan Buckmaster 质疑 OpenAI 是否利用了他与 Anthropic 研究人员 Levent Alpöge 在 Codex 中的项目数据。OpenAI 称求解过程没有访问具体用户数据，但不能完全排除去标识化使用数据曾参与模型改进；双方公开的证明所针对的问题也并不相同。
这份候选解尚未经过全球数学界的独立检验。按克莱数学研究所规则，一项解答需先在合格出版物发表，至少经过两年严格审查并获得广泛认可，才会进入奖项考虑程序。OpenAI 称无意为该结果申请奖项。

两部门要求车企定期报告供应商账期，重点企业每年接受评估
https://s3.ifanr.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/lark2pad-1788912956129-3.png!720
工业和信息化部、市场监管总局 9 月 7 日发布通知，进一步规范汽车企业向供应商支付采购货物、工程和服务等款项。车企需建立供应商账款支付管理制度，并在每年 7 月底和次年 1 月底前分别提交半年度、年度执行情况报告。

招聘集中在服务端开发和 Agent 弹性计算研发两类岗位。前者覆盖大模型研究平台、Agent 框架组件、研发效率基建、DeepSeek API、线上服务和数据工程；后者包括平台开发维护与底层系统调优。本轮没有单列 AI 研究岗位。

高通将提供 SerDes、光学 DSP、低功耗计算和系统集成能力，用于提升数据中心内部高带宽互联。亚马逊则提供云端 AI 基础设施，双方希望在计算、存储、网络带宽和能效之间形成一套可扩展方案。
高通还计划扩大对 AWS AI 基础设施和 Amazon Bedrock 的使用，把它们用于电子设计自动化工作负载，以缩短芯片设计周期。

Meta 发布个人 AI Agent Muse，可持续代办邮件、旅行和购物
https://images.ifanr.cn/wp-content/themes/ifanr-5.0-pc/static/images/ifanrqrcode.jpg
Meta 9 月 8 日发布个人 AI Agent Muse。用户可在独立应用或 WhatsApp 中与它对话，让其拆解目标、制定计划，并在用户关闭应用后继续执行任务。
Muse 由 Muse Spark 模型驱动，可打开浏览器、填写表单、发送邮件、预订旅行和完成购物。它还能连接 Instagram 等 Meta 产品与第三方应用，例如将用户保存的食谱 Reels 整理成采购清单，或在宴请前根据宾客饮食偏好生成菜单。
为隔离 Agent 与用户数据，Meta 为每个 Muse 配置专用云端 Muse Secure VM，并让一个与主 Agent 系统隔离的 Sentinel 审查对外请求。发送邮件、付款等敏感动作需用户确认，账号密码和支付信息存入独立安全区，Muse 本身无法查看。用户可选择关联的应用和权限，也可退出将互动用于模型训练。
Muse 已在美国面向 iOS、Android 和网页用户陆续开放，后续将登陆 Meta AI 眼镜。基础功能主要免费，Meta 同时准备面向高强度使用者的订阅方案。
Robinhood 首次进入 IPO 承销团，参与 Oura 上市
智能戒指公司 Oura 向美国证券交易委员会提交的招股书显示，Robinhood 已进入其 IPO 承销商名单，与高盛、摩根士丹利、摩根大通、Allen \& Company 和 Jefferies 等机构共同参与发行。《华尔街日报》称，这是 Robinhood 第一次正式担任 IPO 承销商。
Robinhood 从 2021 年开始向散户客户分配新股，但过去主要承担分销角色。进入承销团后，它能更早参与发行安排，也有机会在留给平台客户的份额上获得更大发言权。Oura 计划以「OURA」为股票代码在纳斯达克上市，招股书尚未填入发行价和发行股数。
这次安排也让 Robinhood 从面向散户的交易平台进一步进入传统投行业务。不过，Oura 面向员工及指定人士的定向配售项目仍由摩根士丹利管理，Robinhood 的具体承销份额尚未公布。
Mistral 完成 30 亿欧元 D 轮融资，投后估值超 210 亿欧元
https://s3.ifanr.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/lark2pad-1788912961682-8.png!720
法国 AI 公司 Mistral 9 月 8 日宣布完成 30 亿欧元 D 轮融资，投后估值超过 210 亿欧元。公司称，这是欧洲科技公司迄今完成的最大单轮股权融资。
本轮融资由三星电子领投，EQT 管理的 Scaleup Europe Fund 与现有投资者 PSG Equity 共同领投；Advent、贝莱德管理的基金和卢森堡大公国加入投资，ASML、英伟达、a16z、法国公共投资银行、Salesforce Ventures 等现有股东继续跟投。
Mistral 表示，资金将用于前沿模型研究、训练算力、基础设施扩建，以及商业和国际业务增长。公司目前在 20 个国家开展业务，为空中客车、ASML、汇丰等超过 125 家企业提供 AI 服务。
💡 梁琛奇：AI 娱乐产品要让消费过程实时使用算力
https://s3.ifanr.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/lark2pad-1788912963462-9.png!720
字节跳动前 AI 产品团队 Flow 负责人梁琛奇接受《晚点》采访时表示，AI 娱乐产品若只降低内容生产成本，产出的短剧、漫画或视频仍会回到既有平台；新的独立平台需要让用户在消费过程中实时与模型互动，并获得过去不存在的长尾反馈。
他把 AI 娱乐的成立条件归纳为成本、模态和用户习惯。DeepSeek-R1 之后，推理成本继续下降；图片和视频模型跨过可用门槛；用户也已经通过 ChatGPT、豆包等产品学会与 AI 交互。基于这些变化，他判断娱乐产品可以从静态生成转向一边消费、一边生成图片、视频或玩法。
梁琛奇创办的「动念引线」正在同时开发和测试七八个产品，由一两人的小组在两周至一个月内做出 Demo，再按真实用户信号决定关停或追加资源。其首款产品「松果时刻」可把照片和文字扩展为带配音、配乐和简单动画的多图故事；团队下一步会把内容收向特定人群，并尝试让消费端也实时调用模型。
